title: Weak solution descent
statement: For any injective local map $R\to S$ of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction fields $E\subseteq Q$ and finite field extension $E'/E$ [def-pc-field-extension], let $R'$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $E'$ and $S'$ that of $S$ in $(Q\otimes_E E')_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Call $E'/E$ a weak solution if, for every maximal ideal $q$ of $S'$, its contraction $n$ in $R'$ is maximal, $R'_n,S'_q$ are discrete valuation rings, and $nS'_q=qS'_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Reduction is quotient by nilpotents; finite means finite-dimensional; local means pulling back the maximal ideal. Let $A\to B\to C$ be injective local maps of complete DVRs, with fraction fields $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$, and $M/L$ finite [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $K_1/K$ be finite. (i) If $K_1/K$ is a weak solution for $A\to C$, it is a weak solution for $A\to B$. (ii) If $K_1/K$ is a weak solution for $A\to B$ and $K_2/K_1$ is finite and is a weak solution for $A_1\to (C_1)_q$ for every maximal ideal $q$ of $C_1$, then $K_2/K$ is a weak solution for $A\to C$. Here $A_1$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$ and $C_1$ that of $C$ in $(M\otimes_KK_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$. In particular these are finite products of complete DVRs (and $A_1$ is a DVR). More precisely, normalization commutes with composition of these reduced field base changes branchwise: for finite $K_2/K_1/K$, normalizing a branch of $(M\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$ further over $K_2$ gives the corresponding branch of $(M\otimes_K K_2)_{\mathrm{red}}$. The same statement holds for its intermediate lower DVRs. Thus if $K_1$ solves $A\to B$, and $K_2/K_1$ solves $A_1\to(C_1)_q$ for just one maximal ideal $q$, every final branch lying over this $q$ has ramification index one over the integral closure of $A$ in $K_2$; no assertion about the other branches is made.

proof.text: Write $A_i$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $K_i$, $L_i=(L\otimes_KK_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$, $M_i=(M\otimes_KK_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and $B_i,C_i$ for the integral closures of $B,C$ in these rings. The finite case of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], applied to $A\to B$ and $A\to C$, gives the nonempty finite field decompositions and the maximal contractions and local DVR maps from $A_i$. Each field factor is finite over the original upper field: it is a quotient of a tensor algebra spanned by a finite basis of $K_i/K$. An element of a finite product is integral over the base ring exactly when each coordinate is: for the reverse implication multiply their finitely many monic annihilating polynomials. Thus the normalization is the product of the coordinate normalizations. Fix a coordinate: a complete DVR $R$ (one of $A,B,C$) with fraction field $E$, a finite extension $F/E$ (also $F=K_i$ for $R=A$), and the integral closure $N$ of $R$ in $F$. As $R$ is a principal ideal domain it is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], so [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata] makes $R=R/(0)$ N-2: $N$ is a finite $R$-module. Being a domain, $N$ is local and complete by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product]. $R$ has dimension one: a nonzero prime contains some $ut^n$, $n\geq1$, by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], hence the uniformizer $t$. So [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-local-dvr] gives a maximal $q\subset N$ over $\mathfrak m_R$ with $N_q$ a DVR of fraction field $F$ and $\mathfrak m_{N_q}\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$; $N$ being local, $q$ is its maximal ideal, every $s\notin q$ is a unit, and $N=N_q$. Hence $A_i$ is a finite complete DVR and $B_i,C_i$ are finite products of finite complete DVR extensions of $B,C$, local over them. Their localizations at maximal ideals are exactly these coordinate DVRs.

Since $M/L$ is finite, the coordinate argument of step 1 for $B\subset M$ shows that the integral closure $C'$ of $B$ in $M$ is a DVR with fraction field $M$, finite over $B$, and $\mathfrak m_{C'}$ is the only prime of $C'$ over $\mathfrak m_B$ [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata, lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product]. As a principal ideal domain $C$ is normal [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], so $C'\subseteq C$. The prime $\mathfrak m_C\cap C'$ lies over $\mathfrak m_B$ because $B\to C$ is local; hence it is $\mathfrak m_{C'}$. If $x\in C\setminus C'$, write $x=a/b$ with $a=ut'^m$, $b=vt'^n$ for a uniformizer $t'$ of $C'$ [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]; then $m<n$ and $x^{-1}=(v/u)t'^{n-m}\in\mathfrak m_{C'}\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$, impossible for $x\in C$. So $C=C'$; in particular $C$ is integral over $B$. The map $L\otimes_KK_1\to M\otimes_KK_1$ is injective: choose an $L$-linear projection $M\to L$ taking $1$ to $1$ and tensor it with $K_1$ to obtain a left inverse as a linear map. An injective ring map reflects nilpotence, so it induces an injection $L_1\hookrightarrow M_1$. A monic equation over $B$ for an element of $B_1$ remains a monic equation over $C$, giving $B_1\hookrightarrow C_1$. Every element of $C_1$ is integral over $C$, hence over $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive], and therefore over $B_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] every maximal ideal $p$ of $B_1$ has a prime above it in $C_1$; [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal] makes this prime maximal. Conversely [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal] makes the contraction of each maximal $q\subset C_1$ maximal. Hence all the corresponding maps $(B_1)_p\to(C_1)_q$ are injective local maps of DVRs.

Assume (i)'s weak-solution hypothesis and fix any maximal $p\subset B_1$. Choose a maximal $q\subset C_1$ above it by step 2 and put $D=(B_1)_p$, $T=(C_1)_q$. These fit into local injections $A_1\to D\to T$. Choose uniformizers $a,d,t$ of these DVRs. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] write $a=ud^e$ in $D$ and $d=vt^f$ in $T$, with $u,v$ units and $e,f\geq1$; the exponents are positive because the maps are local and injective. Thus $a=uv^e t^{ef}$ in $T$. The hypothesis says $aT=tT$. If $ef\geq2$, expressing $t$ as a multiple of $a$ and cancelling the nonzero $t$ would put $1$ in $tT$, a contradiction. Hence $e=f=1$, so $aD=dD$. Since $p$ was arbitrary, all branches for $A\to B$ satisfy the weak-solution condition, proving (i).

proof.text: For the successive coefficient extensions, let $Q$ denote any of the original upper fields $L,M$ and put $Q_1=(Q\otimes_KK_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$. There is a canonical isomorphism $$(Q_1\otimes_{K_1}K_2)_{\mathrm{red}}\simeq(Q\otimes_KK_2)_{\mathrm{red}}.$$ Here is the argument rather than an assumption that tensor products remain reduced. Maps from either ring to a reduced commutative ring $T$ amount to compatible ring maps $Q\to T$ and $K_2\to T$ agreeing on $K$: on the left, first restrict the latter map to $K_1$, use the tensor universal property, and note that every nilpotent must map to zero. These constructions give inverse homomorphisms; on pure tensors they agree with $$(x\otimes a)\otimes b\longmapsto x\otimes ab.$$ These tensors generate, so both composites are identities. The same construction respects the maps induced by $L\to M$ and the lower field maps, since each sends every pure tensor to the same product.

Decompose $Q_1=\prod_j F_j$ as in step 1. The finite product decomposition induces $$ (Q_1\otimes_{K_1}K_2)_{\mathrm{red}}\simeq\prod_j(F_j\otimes_{K_1}K_2)_{\mathrm{red}}.$$ Explicitly the inverse of the coordinate map sends a pure tensor in the $j$th factor to its tensor multiplied by the coordinate idempotent $e_j$; the identities $\sum e_j=1$ and $e_je_h=0$ for $j\ne h$ check the inverse and multiplication. Nilpotence is coordinatewise in a finite product, so the map passes to reductions. Each right hand factor is again a nonempty finite product of fields, by the finite case of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure] for the complete coordinate DVR of step 1 and the coefficient extension $K_2/K_1$. Consequently the fields of the direct $K_2$-base change are exactly those obtained by base changing each $K_1$-branch, with its parent branch recorded by $e_j$.

Fix a field factor $F$ of $M_1$ and let $D$ be the integral closure of $C$ in $F$, namely the corresponding complete DVR $(C_1)_q$ of step 1. For any factor $H$ of $(F\otimes_{K_1}K_2)_{\mathrm{red}}$, an element $h\in H$ is integral over $D$ if and only if it is integral over $C$. Indeed one direction is [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive], as $D$ is integral over $C$; the other follows by regarding the same monic equation over $C$ as one over $D$. Thus the normalization of $D$ in $H$ equals the normalization of $C$ in $H$. Likewise the normalization of $A_1$ in $K_2$ equals $A_2$, because $A_1$ is integral over $A$. Applied with $B$ instead of $C$, this argument gives the same compatibility for each lower branch. Together with the explicit identifications in steps 4 and 5 this proves the stated branchwise compatibility of successive normalized base changes, including all structural maps.

For (ii), take any maximal ideal of $C_2$ and its coordinate field $H$. By steps 4 and 5 it has one parent $F$ in $M_1$, hence one maximal ideal $q$ of $C_1$. By step 6 its coordinate DVR is precisely the normalization in $H$ occurring in the definition of a weak solution for $A_1\to(C_1)_q$, and the lower normalization is $A_2$. The assumed weak-solution equality for $K_2/K_1$ therefore says exactly that its maximal ideal is generated by the maximal ideal of $A_2$. Step 1 gives the required DVRs and maximal contractions. This proves (ii). If the hypothesis is imposed only at one specified $q$, the identical argument applies to exactly the final branches with that parent, proving the last assertion. No further-extension stability of weak solutions is used. In fact the weak-solution assumption for $A\to B$ is unnecessary for (ii) once the stated assumptions on $A_1\to(C_1)_q$ hold; keeping it gives precisely the requested implication.
